newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken MD says has no plans to resign.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken MD says has no plans to resign.

text.p: S-E-Banken managing director Bjorn Svedberg said on Tuesday he did not plan to leave his position next year when he reaches the age of 60, the date at which his contract stipulates he should step down.

"I hope to be able to continue for a while longer. They will probably have to carry me out of the bank, because I plan on staying. It must be the most enjoyable job a person could have," Svedberg told reporters at a press seminar.
Svedberg said S-E-Banken was prepared for possible Swedish membership of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"We have an aggressive strategy to meet reduced cross trade in European currencies in connection with EMU.
"It will be very important to have enough financial muscle to carry out major European financing deals, something we already can do for the most part," he said.
Svedberg said EMU would initially result in lower income for the bank, but its customer base and financial strength would be enough to cover this loss.
Svedberg said that by the year end, S-E-Banken would launch banking services on the Internet which would enable customers to buy shares, check account balances and transfer money between accounts.

Svedberg said he expected restructuring on the Swedish financial market. He said S-E-Banken had made preliminary calculations regarding an acquisition of state-controlled mortgage institute Stadshypotek, and would be interested when it is put up for sale.
However, he pointed out that this would not take place in the near future since a parliamentary decision was needed before the state could sell its shares.
Svedberg said he shared Nordbanken managing director Jacob Palmstierna's opinion that synergies from restructuring in the sector would be felt foremost on local banking markets.

"Profits from a merger would mean making local branches more effective. This means that the advantages on the cost side would not be as clear in the case of cooperation with a foreign bank where costs on the branch side do not overlap."
